newsitem.title: HUNGARY: RISING MAIZE FUTURES DOMINATE HUNGARY'S BCE TRADE.
newsitem.headline: RISING MAIZE FUTURES DOMINATE HUNGARY'S BCE TRADE.

text.p: Rising maize futures dominated on the Budapest Commodity Exchange's grains section on Wednesday, the penultimate day of 1996 trade.
"A number of brokerages are spreading the 1997 March maturity for more distant deliveries," said Robert Monostori of brokerage Agrimpex.
Maize futures rose by 380 forints to 19,600 for March 1997 and by 100 forints for May and July 1997 to end at 19,500 and 20,100 forints respectively.
"Some companies are closing their positions, others are opening new ones, so the picture is fairly mixed," he said.
Monostori added that fresh supply of wheat and maize could hit the market at the beginning of 1997.
"Maize and wheat quantities that have not yet been sold would appear on the market next year," he said.
Milling wheat prices rose for all maturities except July and August 1997. March 1997 closed at 27,600 forints, May ended at 28,000 forints, both up 400.
Total turnover of the BCE grain section was a below-average 640 million forints, or 1,540 lots, of which 1,044 lots were maize and 411 milling wheat.
(Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts. $1=164.09 forints)
